editorial:
The Love Parade is Ernst Lubitsch's first American sound film, released by Paramount Famous Lasky Corporation on November 19, 1929, starring Maurice Chevalier as the scandal-prone Count Alfred Renard and Jeanette MacDonald in her screen debut as Queen Louise of Sylvania. Nominated for six Academy Awards including Best Picture, it established the template for the Hollywood musical comedy and introduced the Lubitsch Touch to sound cinema. The underlying 1929 film â€” its nine original songs (music by Victor Schertzinger, lyrics by Clifford Grey), script, and photography â€” entered the US public domain on January 1, 2025, when the maximum 95-year US copyright term from its 1929 publication date ran out. The Internet Archive (identifier: the-love-parade-1929, Public Domain Mark 1.0) hosts an earlier transfer that is genuinely free to download and reuse.

The rights trap is Universal Pictures' 2024 4K restoration, produced with The Film Foundation and premiered at the Berlinale Classics section of the 74th Berlin International Film Festival. Universal holds the Paramount library and owns the copyright in that restored master independent of any rights in the 1929 film itself. The Criterion Eclipse Series 8 DVD (2007) similarly embodies a protected transfer. A creator who copies frames or audio from the Universal Blu-ray or a Criterion disc is reproducing a protected restoration, not the free underlying film. Source from the Archive.org upload for commercial reuse; approach Universal for any licensing of the 4K master.
faq: Can I use footage from The Love Parade in my own video, film, or commercial project?

The 1929 film is US public domain â€” its maximum 95-year copyright term expired January 1, 2025. The Internet Archive upload (identifier: the-love-parade-1929, licensed Public Domain Mark 1.0) is the safest free source. Do not rip from the Universal Pictures Blu-ray or the Criterion Eclipse DVD; those specific restorations carry separate copyright in the restored picture and sound, even though the underlying 1929 film is free.
Does Universal Pictures still have rights to The Love Parade?

Universal owns the copyright in its 2024 4K restoration of the film, created with The Film Foundation, and in any earlier transfers it produced. Universal cannot stop someone from using the original 1929 footage drawn from a non-Universal source, but copying the restored picture or audio track from their release infringes the restoration copyright. Universal also markets the film commercially through its catalog, so it is the correct party to contact for any licensing of the 4K master or high-quality press materials.
